metric: Share of faulty query variants (mutants, 14 operators) that targeted databases plus corner cases tell apart from the original, among mutants not proven equivalent and not timed out; the engine's default 8 random databases get 52.7% dev, 11.6% held out, one random seed 11.7% / 4.9%.
correctness: Every kill repeats on both sides on a database respecting NOT NULL and keys (foreign keys not modelled); no kill is counted from a side that disagrees with itself. Survivors not proven equivalent stay in the denominator.
held_out: 69.2% (1,227/1,772 mutants of 22 TPC-H and 19 TPC-C queries; 775 TPC-H mutants timed out and are not in the denominator), strategies fixed on the development split before it was run
caveats: Originals: Calcite, Spark, a 16-query university set (dev) and TPC-H, TPC-C (held out); 28 originals are unsupported (DuckDB rejects them) and not counted. Rerun after the BigQuery-on-DuckDB guards (#446, #469, #633) with nothing else running: 667 dev originals run (623 before: the inline-table queries run again and more translate), so the dev score moved from 71.8% to 83.2% largely because 477 more, mostly easy, mutants are scored, not because a strategy improved. Held-out kills are 1,227 against 1,244 before: 8 of them ended in 'error' (a division by a zero divisor fails in BigQuery, so the database is skipped), 8 in 'timeout', and 'timeout' rose overall from 585 to 775 because the guards cost time per row on TPC-H joins; timeouts leave the denominator, which is why the held-out percentage rose while kills fell. Per mutant against the commit before #446 on the same machine, no mutant went from killed to survived. Mutants are generated, not hand-labelled; 'proven' = proven equivalent mutants (excluded from the score), 'refuted' = killed by any strategy, 'unknown' = survived and not proven equivalent (many are DISTINCT toggles that are equivalent but unprovable), 'timeout' = queries over the 90 s per-query budget (all TPC-H), 'error' = invalid mutants. Strategy details were tuned on the development split. Median counterexample is 3 rows (random 8 databases: 38). Counterexample minimization was not rerun.
